title: Hearing visiting bands in Minneapolis theatres
summary: Little live music was available, but Ben Bernie, Coon-Sanders, Vincent Lopez and Paul Whiteman came to the theatres.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, these are the records you mentioned that you were listening to. What kind of people did you hear live? Anything that...?
You didn't hear much live in them days.
You didn't go around and hear...?

No, wasn't nowhere to go to. People would come around every now and then. I mean, they'd come to... Well, we'd always go... Like, if a band, when we was in Minneapolis, came to the theatres... Like, Ben Burnie(?) came there, and Coon & Saunders...
Yeah. Those bands would come to theatres. Because Paul Whiteman came around, he was supposed to be the King of Jazz. He had Bix and Frankie and them all in his band then.
Well, that was a little later on, right?
Yeah, something like that. '27... Frank and them..> That's when Bix came up with him, in '27.
